teaching.hint: Can a sample remain uniform as one more node is encountered?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A one-item sample can be updated online: replace it at the `t`th node with probability `1/t`.
solution_outline.approach: Store the head. For each call, scan nodes once, replacing the saved value with probability reciprocal to the number seen so far; return the final saved value.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: After visiting `t` nodes, each visited node is represented by the saved value with probability exactly `1/t`.
solution_outline.correctness: The new node enters with probability `1/t`; any earlier node survives with probability `(1/(t-1))*(1-1/t)=1/t`. Induction establishes uniformity after the full list.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time per call and `O(1)` auxiliary space, including for unknown list length.
solution_outline.pitfall: Uniformity is over nodes, so repeated values must not be deduplicated or reweighted.

common_wrong_turns: Sampling distinct values instead of nodes
Assuming the list length is known
source_fidelity_notes: Removed nondeterministic sample outputs; retained node-level uniformity and the unknown-length constant-space follow-up.
